business: Little Shore Play Cafe (a Montessori-inspired play cafe in Salisbury, MD)
why_not: I'd take the free visit to look, but $14 a visit adds up fast on our budget when the library and the park are free. I'm not paying for a membership on a place I haven't seen.

I'd go for the free first visit, but $14 a kid adds up fast with two little ones on one shift-work paycheck, and a monthly membership is out of the question. The library and the free park do the job for nothing.
We do the zoo on Saturdays because it's free, and I only have weekends. I'd probably grab the free first visit, but paying $14 a kid for a play cafe feels like a lot when the zoo costs nothing.

I work full time, so it's Saturdays only, and I already do free library storytime on Tuesdays. I'd grab the free first visit, but I wouldn't commit money before seeing it, and I'll be chasing my kid anyway so the coffee isn't much of a draw.
why_yes: I'm always looking for somewhere indoors to take my toddler, and the free first visit plus the posted cleaning log and shoes-off rule take the edge off my worry about her licking everything. I'd try it for free, and if it feels clean I'd pay for a couple of drop-ins, not a membership yet.

The posted daily cleaning log, shoes off, the 25-kid cap and the gated Baby Nook for my 10-month-old are what I'd look for first. The free first visit lets me check it myself before spending anything, and my 4-year-old would like the pretend market.

I'd take the free first visit, and if my toddler likes it I'd pay the $14 drop-in once because the coffee is included and I could get a little work done. We'd only go once or twice a month, so I'd never do a membership.

The free first visit costs me nothing, so I'd take both kids once and see. I wouldn't pay $45 plus $20 for the sibling when storytime and the parks are free, but a 5-visit pack at $55 might come later if the baby nook is good on a rainy day.
I'd take the free first visit on a Saturday and probably pay for a drop-in after that if my kid liked it, since coffee is included. We'd only go once or twice a month, so no membership for us.

I'm home with the kids all week and rainy or hot days are brutal, so a calm indoor spot with coffee and a free first visit is worth trying. I'd pay drop-in for a couple of visits, but I wouldn't commit to a membership until I see how it feels.
flip: A free visit that shows the Baby Nook really keeps the bigger kids out and the room stays calm, plus a cheaper weekday-morning drop-in around $8 to $10 that fits around our shifts.
A drop-in of around $8 per child with a sibling discount that really cuts the cost, or a rainy-day pack that works out under $6 a visit.
If the Group Mornings at $8 a kid really worked for my moms group and a few other families committed to coming, I'd organize one and pay for that.
Opening close to me with real reviews from other parents, plus a drop-in price around $8-10 a child, or a pack bringing each visit under $9.
A much lower drop-in, like $6-7 a kid, or a free-entry day each month. I'd also need to hear a few other moms say it was worth it.
A quiet, separate under-2 time slot on Saturdays or a way to book a spot with a small capped group, so I know the baby won't get run over.
A Saturday or rainy-day price closer to $8 a kid, or a family cap per visit, and the free first visit turning out great.
A great free first visit on a Saturday where my kid actually wants to go back, plus a drop-in or pack price that works for weekend-only use.
A flat drop-in around $5 to $6 for the first kid, or a free-with-purchase deal on shift days when the parks are too hot or rainy.
A cheaper pack or a Groupon-style deal, say 5 visits for about $40 that doesn't expire quickly, after a free visit my kids actually love.
A party package clearly cheaper or easier than CoCo's, or a drop-in price under about $10 per child with the free first visit proving it's actually calmer and cleaner.
A much lower drop-in price (around $8 for the first child) or a free or cheap open-play hour, so it's not a $20+ outing for two kids.
A cheaper sibling or under-2 price, or a weekday pass for the two of us under about $35 a month, and being close enough that the drive isn't a big gas cost.
